answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor their identity via cryptographic attestation chains backed by zero-knowledge proofs. Registering duplicate agents requires staking escalating collateral inside a staking vault, where costs surge superlinearly as $C(n) = k \cdot n^2$. Even if an attacker stakes cheap copper commodity tokens, the exponential capital exhaustion rapidly makes deploying an adversarial Sybil swarm mathematically unprofitable.
